## Problem

After Gerrit change 1560 merged the bounded completion policy, a normal close verification for bug 0707 produced one false unmet criterion. The verifier claimed tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py contained only a COMMIT steering notice. The actual merged file contains normal Python imports, test functions, and assertions.

## Proven observation

The completion wrapper returns COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE to every losing governed call in a same-response batch (src/rebar/llm/completion_tool_policy.py:153-154). In the observed close run, the model treated that synthetic steering result as if it were the read_file payload and concluded the target file itself was the notice. This is distinct from 0707's zero-bank exhaustion: progress was banked and the close returned a normal FAIL, but evidence fidelity was wrong.

## Plan

- Reproduce with a deterministic or repeated behavioral oracle where a read_file call loses a governed batch and the criterion still requires that file.
- Distinguish tool-result attribution from general model hallucination by varying only the synthetic result contract.
- Design an affirmative, schema-compatible steering result that cannot be scored as repository content, preserving all existing tool schemas and completion vocabulary.
- Prove RED then GREEN and cover primary/successor parity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A held-out oracle reproduces the verifier treating a suppressed governed call's steering result as repository evidence.
- [ ] Losing batch calls remain non-executing while their results are unambiguously classified as steering, not file/search/list content.
- [ ] Completion criteria backed by a real merged file are not marked unmet solely because their concurrent read was suppressed.
- [ ] Existing finite banking, fallback, schemas, CLI/MCP/library surfaces, workflow/environment names, and old vocabulary remain compatible.
- [ ] Focused completion tests, live behavioral coverage, lint, typecheck, and full CI pass.
compiled_state.title: Completion verifier can mistake COMMIT steering for repository file content
